speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn with yellowish discoloration of the skin; this suggests jaundice. To determine the cause and severity, how many hours old were you when the yellowing first appeared, and are you feeding well?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (physiologic jaundice exacerbated by insufficient intake). The infant is 5 days old with jaundice spreading to the trunk, born term via uncomplicated delivery, and exclusively breastfed, which fits the clinical picture of inadequate caloric intake leading to dehydration and prolonged bilirubin clearance.
